title: Filing a detailed slice takes promote plus one edit per section

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`promote` seeds empty sections; `edit` replaces exactly one section. The only way to
create a slice with populated bodies in one shot is a whole `import` outline file. So an
agent filing one fully-specified item runs `add`, `set --depends-on`, `promote`, then
`edit --section Why`, `edit --section Files`, `edit --section Implement` — six or more
process invocations, each re-invalidating the render. This is the biggest agent-workflow
tax not already on the roadmap.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` — `cmd_promote` or a new option
- `src/slicer/ops.py` — populate sections at promote time

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. Promoting from a section-bearing source populates the slice in one command.
2. A read counterpart to `edit --section` returns one section's body.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Let `promote` take a source that fills sections in one call — reuse the outline section
parser rather than inventing a second format — and add `show --section NAME` as the read
counterpart to `edit --section`. Together an agent writes and reads a slice without the
6-call dance.

**Not in this slice:** `edit --append` (S17) and multi-section edit of an existing slice.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: An agent files a fully-specified slice in one or two commands.
